source.title: Junior School Curriculum Design: Hindu Religious Education, Grade 9
source.notes: Filename confirmed against KICD's own Google Drive listing (kicd.ac.ke/cbc-materials/curriculum-designs/grade-nine-designs/, file id 1ePaw7pIrLG3AjX2mbTXIEimXTRnkdfuC, whose /preview page title reads 'HRE Grade 9 - July 2024 - Fin.pdf'). WebFetch reported 'unable to extract meaningful content' on the PDF itself but saved it locally; Read then parsed the full PDF text natively (ISBN 978-9914-43-438-5, First Published 2023). Strand/sub-strand headings, SLOs, and key inquiry questions below are transcribed verbatim. NOTABLE: the subject's own general learning outcomes describe HRE as covering four faith traditions (Sanatan/Vedic, Jain, Buddhist, and Sikh), but every sub-strand actually detailed in this specific Grade 9 design is Sikh-specific (Sikh Scriptures, Sikh Principles of Dharma, Sikh Sanskaars, etc.) — not an error, just this grade's rotation within the broader multi-faith HRE syllabus (Grade 7's HRE design, by contrast, is titled 'Hindu Religious Education' generically per its own filename).

subStrands.name: Enlightened Beings
subStrands.notes: Covers Tridev's contribution to mankind, the Tirthankars' way of non-violence (Ahimsa), Buddha's gift to humanity, and the Guru's way of life (Khalsa Panth) — i.e. one representative figure/teaching from each of the four HRE faith traditions.
specificLearningOutcomes: State the contributions of the Enlightened Beings for harmonious living
Narrate Scriptural stories that portray the teachings of the Enlightened Beings for moral and social development
Desire to implement the teachings of the Enlightened Beings for personal improvement
keyInquiryQuestions: How have the teachings of the Enlightened Beings impacted society?
How do the life histories of Enlightened Beings guide our lives today?

subStrands.name: Scriptural Text and Role of Sikh Scriptures
subStrands.notes: Covers Sri Sukhmani Sahib in Sri Guru Granth Sahib ji, and Ashtpadi from 17-24.
specificLearningOutcomes: Outline the role of Sikh Scriptures for guidance in one's life
Explain the compilation of Sri Sukhmani Sahib in Sri Guru Granth Sahib ji for internalisation
Interpret the universal message embedded in the Sri Sukhmani Sahib for deeper understanding
Appreciate the teachings of the Sikh Scriptures for spiritual development
keyInquiryQuestions: How do the Scriptures influence your lifestyle?
How does the recitation of the Scriptures help to acquire self-efficacy?

subStrands.name: Sikh Principles of Dharma
subStrands.notes: Covers Compassion (Daya), Satisfaction (Santokh), Truth (Sat), Humility (Nimrata), Love (Pyaar), Naam Japnaa, Honest livelihood (Kirat Karni), Sharing (Vand ke Chhakna).
specificLearningOutcomes: State the Sikh Principles of Dharma for knowledge
Describe the concepts of the three pillars of Sikh Dharma for spiritual uplift
Display the Sikh Principles of Dharma in a school environment
Appreciate the Sikh Principles of Dharma for character development
keyInquiryQuestions: How are the Sikh Principles of Dharma still relevant in today's age?
How does the implementation of the Sikh Principles of Dharma uplift your spirituality?

subStrands.name: Rituals and Protocols
subStrands.notes: During religious activities: Akhand Ramayan Path, Kalpa Sutra Recitation, Akhand path of Sri Guru Granth Sahib ji, Katha. Body labels this as sub-strand '4.1' in some places and '4.2' in the summary table — transcribed as it appears in the body heading.
specificLearningOutcomes: Enumerate common rituals and protocols during religious practices
Describe the rituals and protocols performed during religious activities for spiritual grounding
Model the mandatory religious etiquette for self-efficacy
Appreciate rituals and protocols performed during religious activities for spiritual growth
keyInquiryQuestions: Why are Sanskaars important in one's life?
How does Katha help to understand spiritual contexts in the four faiths?

subStrands.name: Knowledge (Gyan/Jnan Yog)
subStrands.notes: Covers Hearing (sravana), Thinking (manana), Meditation (nididhyasana); practitioners: Nachiketa, Gautam Swami, Webu Sayadaw, Bhai Gurdas Ji — one practitioner per faith tradition.
specificLearningOutcomes: State the key events of the selected four prominent practitioners of Gyan/Jnana Yog for better understanding
Outline the four key practitioners of Gyan/Jnana Yog from the four faiths for familiarisation
Interpret the importance of Gyan/Jnana Yog as a spiritual path
Acknowledge Gyan/Jnana Yog as a tool of holistic development
keyInquiryQuestions: How relevant is Gyan/Jnana Yog in modern society?
Why are contemplative practices important in our lives?

subStrands.name: Sikh Sanskaars
subStrands.notes: Naming ceremony (naam karan), tying the turban (dastar bandhan), baptism (amrit shakna), marriage (anand karaj), death (antim sanskaar).
specificLearningOutcomes: Outline the five Sanskaars as per Sikh Dharma for familiarisation
Illustrate the significance of the five Sikh Sanskaars for better understanding
Appreciate the Sikh Sanskaars for harmonious living
keyInquiryQuestions: Why does a Sikh need these Sanskaars in their life?
How does Sanskaars connect one with their faith?
